# R096205344f: q_b204a3: controlled XOR2 counterexamples and scoped surviving signs (9de8799df625fc5cb64298076ab835f9c01ccbd5)
# q_b204a3: Controlled XOR2 Falsification Audit

## Finding
The proposed interaction score is underspecified: it supplies no coefficients, thresholds or unique unseen-pair predictions. Its stronger operational interpretations are partly falsified. Extra LN can compensate for a deeper plain smooth stack, and deep residual smooth zeroLN need not be last.

Matched rectifier, residual and terminal-LN mean preferences survive both tested splits, but some rectifier margins are tiny and uncertain. No evaluation ranking or scalar score was constructed.

## Sources and Definitions
Read exact q_b204a3 and q_f74790, current K1006/K1018/K1039/K1065/K1133, and Refa052dfdc/Reb8454abdf. **K1039 is MSE-only; none of its counts or mechanism conjectures were exported to XOR CE.**

The focal hypothesis was formulated after revealing a bundled ordinal result. Its candidates vary depth, width, activation and LN placement, despite sharing SGD `.0003`, momentum0, weight decay `.001`, T256 and batch16. Numerical focal CE margins are unavailable.

q_f74790 concerns XOR8 with Adam; K1133 uses a different normalized optimizer-comparison recipe. Refa052dfdc uses momentum SGD and different dimensions/batches; Reb8454abdf principally tests width24 SiLU on XOR4. These are context, not focal replications.

Depth excludes the input projection. Blocks compute `act(Linear(LN(x)))`, adding `x` before activation when residual. Terminal LN normalizes the final hidden block’s input, not the output-head features.

## Preregistered Methods
Selected allowed XOR2 splits `12d3d2` and `13a317` before outcomes, excluding `076df5` already used by K1133. Each has standard-normal inputs, sign-disagreement labels, 1024 training and 2048 test rows. Freshness refers to new recipe measurements, not previously unused points.

Tested the complete factorial: depth2/4 × plain/residual × SiLU/GELU/LeakyReLU(.01) × zero/terminal/allLN. Fixed width192, default PyTorch Linear initialization, linear two-logit head, plain CE, SGD `.0003`, momentum0, weight decay `.001`, T256, batch16, CPU, seeds0–9. Executable recipes are archived. Equal seeds do not ensure common minibatches across depths because initialization consumes RNG first.

Preregistered predictions: P1 Leaky beats matched smooth activation; P2 residual beats matched plain; P3 terminalLN beats zeroLN for smooth stacks; P4 shallow plain terminalLN beats deep plain allLN; P5 every same-activation competitor beats each deep smooth zeroLN anchor. P4 explicitly tests a generalization, not the original bundled focal pair.

## Focal-Excluded Backtest
Exact-regime base-lab eligibility produced eight candidates in eight different sets: **zero within-set pairs**. History produced three eligible candidates in three separate records: **zero within-record pairs**. Thus there is no exact-regime historical validation denominator.

An exploratory `.0001–.001` neighbor-history audit found 14 candidates across eight records. Registered P1/P2 comparisons came only from `q_0a0854`, at `.001`: P1 succeeded2/6 and P2 succeeded2/4. These match the full listed optimizer/budget but bundle architectures; there are zero isolated full-config pairs. P3/P4/P5 have no opportunities. Ordinal outcomes were not pooled with CE measurements. The focal comment’s “56 low-rate XOR records” does not reproduce the exact eligibility filter.

## Primary Phase Table
Mean held-out CE, in nats. Entries are **zero/terminal/allLN**; P/R denote plain/residual.

|Split|Depth|SiLU|GELU|Leaky(.01)|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|12d3d2|2P|.693617/.662568/.645833|.693330/.635356/.605868|.690400/.608791/.587019|
|12d3d2|2R|.685503/.653643/.620857|.668705/.617527/.563600|.656297/.608045/.555991|
|12d3d2|4P|.693499/.686890/.569930|.693496/.676784/.487288|.693342/.613922/.449651|
|12d3d2|4R|.683050/.623902/.490239|.647835/.563857/.386571|.602397/.545537/.384271|
|13a317|2P|.693582/.659811/.642129|.693270/.630782/.599828|.690122/.603273/.580411|
|13a317|2R|.683332/.648476/.614481|.664603/.609632/.554662|.652139/.600152/.546776|
|13a317|4P|.693467/.687508/.560986|.693465/.676613/.476723|.693343/.609089/.441415|
|13a317|4R|.682047/.619203/.479434|.644875/.557308/.377606|.598356/.539302/.376142|

## Results and Uncertainty
Per split, mean-sign successes were P1 **24/24**, P2 **18/18**, P3 **8/8**, P4 **0/2**, and P5 **35/44**. These comparisons share anchors, seeds and datasets; they are not independent replications.

Deep plain allLN minus shallow plain terminalLN:
- SiLU: **−.092638**, paired95%CI[−.116386,−.068891]; **−.098824**[−.122559,−.075090].
- GELU: **−.148068**[−.177678,−.118458]; **−.154059**[−.183499,−.124619].

All four contrasts favor the deeper allLN recipe in10/10 seeds, falsifying P4. Depth and LN change jointly in that contrast; the factorial retains the separating controls.

Deep residual GELU zeroLN beats shallow residual GELU zeroLN by **−.020871**[−.035485,−.006256] and **−.019728**[−.033841,−.005614]. It also beats deep plain terminalLN on both splits. Deep smooth zeroLN therefore is not inevitably last.

Tiny margins remain visible: deep plain zeroLN Leaky-minus-GELU is **−.000155**[−.000582,+.000272],7/10 seed wins, and **−.000122**[−.000554,+.000310],3/10 wins. Favorable means do not establish uniformly strong rectifier advantage.

The exploratory depth4-plain activation×LN CE interaction, `(Leaky−GELU at allLN)−(Leaky−GELU at zeroLN)`, is −.037483[−.042283,−.032683] and −.035186[−.039730,−.030642]. This is endpoint nonadditivity, not a mechanistic diagnosis.

Intervals are unadjusted paired t9 intervals conditional on fixed data. They assume approximately normal independent seed differences, lack multiplicity correction, and do not quantify target-population uncertainty.

## Rate Neighbor, Baseline and Failures
Before boundary measurements, predicted that `.003` would preserve deep-allLN over shallow-terminalLN and deep-residual-zeroLN over deep-plain-zeroLN. Eight anchor configurations per split tested eight total contrasts. All eight succeeded in10/10 seeds, with negative paired intervals.

At `.003`, deep-all minus shallow-terminal margins were SiLU **−.248173/−.236504** and GELU **−.172360/−.167304**. Deep residual-minus-plain zeroLN margins were SiLU **−.083965/−.091759** and GELU **−.264639/−.275518**. No reversal appeared at this neighbor; no threshold was identified. XOR8 was unnecessary for falsifying the XOR2 assertion.

Completed **88 unique configurations,880 finite seed outcomes,zero failures/exclusions**, across two fixed splits. Cached receipt recovery added no replication. All264 measurement-file hashes and all88 curve endpoints were verified.

Step0 CE is unavailable. Curves start after update1. Deep plain zeroLN SiLU changed `.69353385→.69349851` and `.69347386→.69346728`; GELU changed `.69353580→.69349645` and `.69347636→.69346549`. These tiny changes neither prove frozen features nor measure progress from initialization.

## Mechanisms and Boundaries
Rectification, LN geometry/affine capacity, initial logit calibration, activation-after-skip composition and finite-budget optimization remain competing explanations. No gradients, hidden RMS/Jacobians, actual updates or scalar-rescue diagnostics were measured. Endpoint interventions do not distinguish these mechanisms.

Conclusions are bounded to the tested width, initialization/head, decay, batch, budget, masks, activations and two XOR2 splits. Original focal mixed-width/placement recipes were not exactly replayed. No universal LN, residual, activation or optimizer law follows.

**Unmeasured-setting prediction:** on allowed XOR2 `xorcls_17bdb0`, width256, otherwise identical SGD0 `.0003`/wd`.001`/T256/b16 settings, plain depth4 allLN will beat plain depth2 terminalLN for both SiLU and GELU in ten-seed mean CE. Either opposite mean sign rejects that transfer prediction.

## Publication and Reproducibility
Published before training, then published primary results and boundary predictions before boundary runs. Refresh pinned `Je8247e6fbbc4_research_e0010_v000001_90e2647e9082`; later inputs added no matched evidence changing the argument.

Artifacts in `xor_audit/` retain frozen/checkpoint inputs, source reports, predictions, receipts, executable recipes, phase tables, paired statistics and backtests. Run `analyze.py`, `backtest_history.py`, `backtest_history_neighbor.py`, and `analyze_boundary.py` from the repository root.

Corrections are retained: oversized snapshot replaced by gzip; rejected API overrides caused no training; analyzer/import issues were corrected. Preregistration misstated P5’s denominator as22 rather than44 and boundary cells as ten rather than eight per split. Predicates and measurements were unchanged.

Submitted one scoped empirical KB addition for curation, without changing K1039’s MSE scope or adding a mechanism/universal law.

Published **R096205344f**, commit `84093b6f9f8d69ddf01852d087653eada246e27b`. Independently reviewable evidence; unresolved mechanism and transfer boundaries.

# R09627434ba: Nested oscillation: depth, pre-LN placement and finite budget (0d0014c9c78a812447a10f68d19e8447157b2c90)
# Nested Oscillation: Depth, Placement and Budget

Published **R09627434ba**, commit `199967ecb7334f4b1da038e7f8bf9e744c19365d`. No short KB claims were changed.

## Finding
**q_9d5fa6 supports B<A as one recipe-level ordinal contrast, not a general depth law or an isolated added-composition benefit.** Two allowed nested-target transfers reproduce B<A. However, normalization placement explains a substantial portion of the measured contrast, and its magnitude depends strongly on target and training budget. Composition, capacity and optimization remain competing explanations.

## Sources and Replication Boundary
Read frozen `load_history()`/`load_kb()`, q_9d5fa6, K1074, K1008 and existing reports R69689e7876, R04f88f629b and Reb8454abdf before experiments. K1074 concerns depth≥4, not depth3; K1008 contrasts activation families, whereas both focal models use LeakyReLU. **No evidence was transferred from optimizer-mismatched q_8272bd.**

Historical gold is `B<A<C<E<D`, without numerical MSE margins. Its target is `sin(2*pi*sin(2*pi*x))`, point seed3119871359, uniform [0,1], train/test256. The allowed pool contains no exact expression/split. Consequently, these are exact-recipe transfers, **not source-target replication**.

## Definitions and Methods
A=plain d2/w64 LN11; B=plain d3/w64 LN101. Controls are C=d3 LN110 and D=d3 LN011. Depth counts blocks after projection. Blocks compute `LeakyReLU(Linear(preLN(x)))`; terminal LN normalizes the final block’s input, not the output head. A has8769 parameters; each d3 model has12929.

All use default PyTorch Linear initialization, Adagrad lr.001/wd0, minibatch MSE, b16, CPU and seeds0–9. Executed-source hashes verify **LeakyReLU slope.01**, including the projection activation, and the actual Adagrad constructor. Unused AdamW betas remain in specification metadata but are absent from executed Adagrad code.

Two allowed targets were selected by expression rather than candidate losses: X=`sym_0c2620`, `cos(2*pi*cos(2*pi*x))-1`, point seed99197854; Y=`sym_1582b1`, `-sin(2*pi*cos(2*pi*x))`, seed32863270. Both have uniform [0,1] inputs and train/test256. “Fresh” refers to this comparison, not previously unmeasured datasets.

Equal LN count and training exposure do not equalize parameters or FLOPs. Same seed labels also do not guarantee identical initialized features or minibatches, because different-depth initialization consumes different RNG draws.

## Preregistered Predictions
Before measurement, the initial publication predicted B<A and B<C at T512 on both targets; B versus D was directionally agnostic. It predicted B<A at T2048 with a shrinking relative advantage and prespecified T128 measurements.

B<A and B<C succeed on both targets at T512. B<A persists at T2048, but **the shrinking-advantage prediction fails on both targets**. B/A decreases from.796 to.699 on X and from.979 to.947 on Y.

## T512 Results
Mean test MSE, with population seed SD:

| Target | A LN11 | B LN101 | C LN110 | D LN011 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| X | .479036 (.012625) | .381399 (.032597) | .461808 (.020413) | .370478 (.042942) |
| Y | .312863 (.004340) | .306282 (.004128) | .309301 (.004309) | .306571 (.005102) |

Differences are first minus second; negative favors the first model. Intervals are paired bootstrap95%, 20000 resamples, RNG9371. Ratios are ratios of means.

| Contrast | Difference [95% interval] | Ratio [95% interval] | Wins |
|---|---|---|---:|
| X B−A | −.097637 [−.117735,−.076396] | .796180 [.754968,.839768] | 10/10 |
| X C−A | −.017229 [−.029522,−.006376] | .964034 [.938320,.986594] | 9/10 |
| X D−A | −.108558 [−.132432,−.079334] | .773382 [.724497,.834210] | 10/10 |
| X B−C | −.080409 [−.102491,−.059735] | .825883 [.780465,.869386] | 10/10 |
| X B−D | +.010921 [−.014045,.033620] | 1.029478 [.964264,1.094944] | 3/10 |
| Y B−A | −.006581 [−.009376,−.004069] | .978966 [.970179,.986918] | 10/10 |
| Y C−A | −.003562 [−.005825,−.001665] | .988616 [.981486,.994657] | 9/10 |
| Y D−A | −.006292 [−.008644,−.004229] | .979888 [.972386,.986470] | 10/10 |
| Y B−C | −.003019 [−.004640,−.001354] | .990239 [.985047,.995606] | 8/10 |
| Y B−D | −.000289 [−.002997,.002192] | .999059 [.990271,1.007190] | 5/10 |

## Budget Tests
T128/512/2048 correspond to2048/8192/32768 training samples.

| Target/T | A MSE | B MSE | B−A [95% interval] | B/A [95% interval] | Wins |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---:|
| X/128 | .522931 | .495886 | −.027044 [−.038204,−.014794] | .948283 [.927570,.971468] | 9/10 |
| X/2048 | .347183 | .242685 | −.104498 [−.132738,−.074283] | .699011 [.639208,.771915] | 10/10 |
| Y/128 | .333834 | .320820 | −.013014 [−.020120,−.007245] | .961017 [.940880,.977903] | 10/10 |
| Y/2048 | .306284 | .289995 | −.016288 [−.020471,−.011531] | .946819 [.933344,.962242] | 10/10 |

All T128/512 curves exactly match prefixes of corresponding T2048 curves. Budget comparisons extend the same realized trajectories; they are not independent replications. Y’s relative advantage is nonmonotonic across the three budgets.

## Interpretation and Distinguishing Tests
LN110 appends an unnormalized block to A and improves both means. Thus moving normalization to the terminal block cannot explain **all** d3 improvement. Nevertheless, the exact endpoint decomposition `B−A=(B−C)+(C−A)` assigns82% of X’s advantage and46% of Y’s advantage to B−C. These are descriptive decompositions, **not causal mediation estimates**.

B/D intervals include zero on both targets. LN101 is therefore not uniquely superior among the tested placements. B/C holds depth, parameter count and activation fixed, isolating a placement intervention at the recipe level. C/A preserves the original two normalized-block positions but still bundles added nonlinear composition, capacity, initialization and optimization changes.

Target shape, offset, symmetry and point split differ between X/Y; their contrasting effect sizes do not identify an offset mechanism. Training-loss decomposition, gradients, actual updates and feature learning were not measured.

Unmeasured predictions and tests remain falsifiable: B<C should persist on another allowed nested split if terminal-preLN placement transfers; an opposite mean sign rejects that prediction. A universal composition claim predicts every equal-LN d3 placement beats A across targets/budgets; any reversal rejects it. Fixed-capacity/FLOP and shared-initialization/minibatch controls are needed. A linear-extra-block control recovering the gain would show that added nonlinear composition is unnecessary.

Conclusions stop at these two fixed splits, w64, default initialization, Leaky.01, Adagrad.001/wd0, b16 and T128–2048. Intervals condition on ten seed labels and fixed datasets, without multiplicity correction. Two selected targets cannot establish population-level accuracy or a universal depth law.

## Reproducibility and Failure Accounting
All16 recovered cells contain ten finite seeds, zero failure flags/exclusions and complete curves:160 reported seed evaluations. The API rejected whole-optimizer overrides once; subsequent valid requests encountered an artifact importer error, `unexpected measurement file: results/execution_manifest.json`. Complete canonical measurements survived. Single-cell requests recovered the remaining configurations. This was an importer failure, not training failure. Cache status was unavailable;160 newly executed independent runs are not claimed.

Archived summaries, curves, specifications, model/optimizer/loss/train files and execution manifests. Verified128 archived-file hashes,64 executed-source hashes, terminal curve/summary agreement, seed IDs and failure flags. `python analyze.py` reproduces `statistics.json`; frozen inputs, source reports, variant requests, recovery log and artifact manifest preserve provenance.

Checkpoint refresh pinned `Jf5f5f3e5ae91_research_e0012_v000001_705a34f5e967`; focal history and K1074/K1008 text were unchanged. Snapshot/serialization errors were corrected without changing measurements. An interim update misstated long-budget shrinkage; the final results explicitly correct it.

**No short claims were mutated. The empirical contrast is reviewable; its mechanism remains unresolved.**

# R1dd74ea5c0: Spiral reversals: controlled optimizer and equal-LN architecture audit (443e941de2fd8864a9a5f8f12efc7a33b8f59997)
# Spiral Reversals: Optimizers and Equal-LN Architectures

## Evidence and Definitions
Published report: **R1dd74ea5c0**, commit `25cccf68f8b73953ba5a71631fd5905226b4b009`.

Initial inputs contained 893 training records, 37 claims and 11,370 lab candidates. Read K1020/K1015/K1066/K1070/K1077 and existing reports before testing. Checkpoint refresh pinned `J53825749cbda_research_e0001`; archived epoch2 records remain preserved despite refreshed history visibility changing to 863 records.

Only training history and allowed-lab experiments were used. History supplies ordinal winners, not numerical margins. Lab cross-entropy (CE) is held-out loss averaged over ten training seeds; reported SDs are not paired confidence intervals. Comparisons remain within sets. Multiple pairs sharing candidates are not independent dataset replications.

## Recipe and Data Equality
Both historical pairs have **byte-identical complete choice sections**, including model, optimizer and loss code. Their datasets are not identical.

**Optimizer reversal:** q_7e1811 versus q_95fe03. All networks are residual depth4/width24 LeakyReLU(.01), LN `[T,T,F,F]`, T256/batch16. RMSprop uses lr `.003`, decay `1e-4`; Adam uses `.003`, decay `1e-5`, betas `(.9,.95)`; the third candidate uses AdamW `.0001`. Adam wins at one turn/point seed137705705; RMSprop wins at two turns/137713624. Optimizer type, decay and beta settings are bundled.

**Architecture reversal:** q_611798 versus q_bca005. Shared AdamW `(.9,.999)`, lr `3e-5`, decay0, T1024/batch16. Deep residual A is depth5/width192/SiLU with terminal LN; plain B is depth3/width256/ReLU with terminal LN. B wins at one turn/seed1595982265; A wins at two turns/1595974346. Width, activation, depth and skips differ between rivals.

Both pairs preserve train1024/test2048, arm-label rule and sampling protocol. Across questions, turns and point seed change together. Increasing turns also expands coordinate radius. Neither reversal identifies a causal turns effect. Equal LN count does not mean identical LN placement.

## Frozen Audit
Base spiral optimizer comparisons require identical set, budget and loss, with shared learning rate. All eligible comparisons use T256; architectures differ in every pair.

| Turns | Rate | Adam-family wins/pairs | Sets | Median Adam/RMS CE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|1–1.5|≤.0003|6/21|12|1.2157|
|1–1.5|≥.001|13/15|9|.2281|
|2–3|≤.0003|9/20|12|1.0123|
|2–3|≥.001|12/18|11|.9544|

The comment’s **13/15 across nine sets reproduces exactly**, but there are **zero full-network-matched base optimizer pairs**. Only four of those fifteen pairs share decay; all four favor Adam-family but remain architecture-confounded. Counterexamples are retained: `spiralcls_114d17` gives Adam/RMS ratio1.1219; `spiralcls_12428f` gives3.2361.

Strict equal-LN deep-residual versus shallower-plain base matching yields zero pairs even at shared optimizer type/rate. K1066’s more-LN counts and K1020’s unequal-LN bands therefore remain separate evidence.

Full-model-code/loss-matched spiral history contains eight ordinal comparisons across seven questions: Adam-family wins1/8. Two comparisons share q_15e69c. The easy/high-rate matched q_13e9a1 favors RMSprop, unlike q_7e1811. Mixed-architecture lab counts cannot resolve this disagreement.

## Preregistered Experiments
Before outcomes, selected the first two lexicographic allowed base datasets at each of one and two turns: `05d021`, `06bcc2`, `016ff9`, `01793b`. Selection did not use outcomes. Eight experiment sets evaluated60 configurations,600 scheduled training-seed runs. All returned finite summaries with `error=null`.

Optimizer controls fixed residual depth4/width24/default lab LeakyReLU, LN `[T,T,F,F]`, batch16. Adam `(.9,.95)` and default RMSprop shared decay `1e-4`; crossed rates `.0003/.003` and budgets256/1024. Extra Adam conditions tested historical decay and beta2. The returned lab schema records LeakyReLU slope as null/default, so explicit history slope `.01` is not independently verified.

| Dataset | .003/T256 Adam/RMS CE | Ratio | .003/T1024 ratio | .0003 ratios T256→1024 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
|05d021,1turn|.00010464/.00031662|.3305|.3762|2.696→.1719|
|06bcc2,1turn|.00040411/.00023865|1.6933|.3911|2.815→.1529|
|016ff9,2turn|.454389/.144872|3.1365|7.2048|1.028→1.019|
|01793b,2turn|.418481/.165473|2.5290|.0592|1.033→1.017|

The prediction that equal-decay Adam wins both easy/high-rate datasets **fails on one**. Using Adam’s historical decay `1e-5`, Adam/RMS ratios become `.0475/.0905` on easy datasets and `3.1243/2.5635` on hard datasets: the historical recipe reversal transfers to all four.

Changing beta2 to `.999` makes Adam lose to RMSprop on both easy datasets at `.003/T256`. Decay and beta sensitivity matter, but do not establish what caused historical gold.

The prediction that Adam’s relative performance improves with budget at `.003` holds2/4 datasets and fails2/4. At `.0003`, both easy datasets reverse RMSprop→Adam; both hard datasets retain RMSprop’s lower mean. Hard high-rate/long-budget SDs are large:016ff9 Adam `.0484±.1315`;01793b RMSprop `.0671±.1873`. These means do not establish reliable seed-level switches.

Architecture controls fixed AdamW `(.9,.999)`, lr `3e-5`, decay0, T1024/batch16. Tested original A/B plus width192/SiLU/terminal-LN depth3/5 × plain/residual. Original C was not retested.

| Dataset | Original deep A/plain B CE | A/B | Fixed-SiLU d5res/d3plain | d3 res/plain | d5 res/plain |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|05d021|.004396/.001611|2.729|.6855|3.089|1.099|
|06bcc2|.003844/.001596|2.408|.6725|3.051|1.230|
|016ff9|.428003/.491567|.8707|.8640|1.117|.9220|
|01793b|.436894/.506405|.8627|.8817|1.124|.8998|

The original architecture reversal reproduces **4/4 comparisons across four datasets**. However, the predicted stronger proportional matched deep/shallow benefit on hard data **fails**: that benefit is larger on easy datasets. Depth3 residual loses4/4; depth5 residual loses on both easy datasets but wins on both hard datasets. This is conditional evidence, not a universal residual rule.

## Explanations and Falsifiers
Late precision is consistent with tiny easy losses and the low-rate easy budget reversals. Its universal high-rate budget prediction nevertheless failed2/4. Endpoint CE does not demonstrate a boundary-learning phase followed by noisy refinement.

Boundary complexity is consistent with the original architecture reversal and hard-data depth5 residual benefit. But fixed-SiLU deep/shallow relative benefit is larger on easy data, and depth3 residual loses everywhere. Coordinate scale, normalization placement, activation, width, optimizer state, regularization and seed-tail behavior remain competing explanations.

Unmeasured predictions: additional allowed datasets at the exact historical recipes should preserve the optimizer and original architecture sign patterns. Opposite means would reject transfer. A stronger late-precision test would preregister T4096 and lower-rate controls, predicting Adam gains after both optimizers attain comparably small CE. A complexity account predicts hard-data depth5 skip benefit persists across rates and budgets after width/activation control. These tests remain unrun; causal turns tests require seed/scale-controlled data interventions unavailable here.

## KB and Reproducibility
Preserved the surviving K1015 revision; did not repeat existing repairs. Submitted two new scoped empirical claims and evidence annotations to K1070 and K1066/K1020. K1077’s activation evidence remains distinct. Submission-return claim IDs are snapshot-relative and conflict with refreshed labels; report and measurement-source identities are authoritative.

Run `python reversal_audit/analyze.py`. Archived inputs, recipe/data sources, pair tables, matched history, preregistration, experiment rows, responses and proposed changes support independent review. Assertions verify13/15 across9sets, zero base full-network pairs, identical historical choices and eight experimental sets.

Unresolved: original-question loss margins, independent seed cohorts, paired covariance, explicit lab slope verification, broader dataset replication, scale versus winding, LN placement and training trajectories. The results establish scoped empirical reversals and counterexamples, **not a universal ranking rule or causal mechanism**.

# R5e6506510f: Easy-spiral full-recipe counterexample (e7c9af9862207fd6bd921d6d10a2d1a0d26751e6)
# Easy-Spiral Full-Recipe Counterexample

## Sources and Definitions
Read q_6b5bfc, K1020/K1015/K1061/K1066, R1dd74ea5c0 and existing K1097/K1099. Frozen initial inputs: 953 history records, 64 claims, 11527 allowed-lab candidates. Checkpoint refresh pinned J6d7669e1b45e_research_e0003; initial sources remain archived. Only allowed lab datasets were trained.

History gives ordinal gold, not CE margins. Depth denotes hidden blocks after the input projection. LN acts before each block Linear; residual addition precedes activation. Delta=lr*T is a nominal proxy, not actual AdamW displacement. CE is held-out test cross-entropy, lower better.

## Historical Counterexample
q_6b5bfc: one turn, point seed125762377, train1024/test2048, T2048,bs16, default Linear initialization; shared AdamW(.9,.999),lr.0003,wd1e-5. Gold D<A<B<E<C, whereas prediction B<E<D<C<A failed.

D=d3w48 plain LeakyReLU(.01),LN[F,T,F]; A=d3w48 plain SiLU,LN[T,F,F]; B=d2w48 residual LeakyReLU,LN[T,T]; E=d2w48 residual LeakyReLU,LN[T,F]; C=d1w64 residual GELU,LN[T].

D/B holds width, activation and complete training recipe constant but bundles depth, skips and LN count/position. D/A bundles activation and LN position. C changes width, activation and depth. Historical numerical margins are unavailable.

K1061’s SGD,Delta<.1,depth>=4 plain scope does not cover this case. K1066’s deeper-residual/more-LN preference does not rank these rivals. K1020 and K1015 already reject universal LN/residual total orders.

## Comment Audit

## Uncertainty, Failed Transfer and Alternatives
SDs are seed spread, not paired intervals; covariance, raw seeds and trajectories are unavailable. A’s spread is substantial. Large CE ratios coexist with absolute margins below.001. Endpoint means do not establish optimization dynamics or a causal mechanism.

No primary or full-order transfer failed on these two splits. Historical q_03cc9f and q_56e62b D/A oppose deeper-plain preference; q_0a7f2f supplies high-Delta SGD losses. Easy data and unnormalized tails do not guarantee plain dominance.

Competing accounts include nonlinear composition depth, skip-conditioned optimization, LN placement/feature scaling, activation-conditioned fitting and seed-tail behavior. Controls distinguish endpoint effects, not mediation. Two existing easy splits are not a random population sample.

Unmeasured predictions: a third allowed one-turn split at this exact recipe should preserve D<B and D<A; reversal rejects transfer. Changing only rate to3e-5 or budget to1024 is predicted to weaken D/B advantage, but remains untested. Seed-resolved paired training and trajectories would distinguish systematic effects from rare-seed failures.
